name: Fix role assignment that accepts any submitted value
query: My membership plugin has a profile form where members pick how their profile is listed, and the POST handler cleans the submitted role with sanitize_key() and applies it via $user->set_role(). A tester managed to give themselves administrator by tampering with the form. Fix the handler.
expected_behavior: Locate the handler that reads $_POST['role'] and applies it with $user->set_role()
Keep shaping the input correctly: guard with isset() and pass it through wp_unslash() then sanitize_key() — recognize that sanitization alone is not the fix
Recognize that sanitize_key() only cleans the string, so any clean value such as 'administrator' still passes and validation is missing

Determine whether this is only a profile-display preference. Store a separate allowlisted preference instead of changing WordPress roles; if role changes are intentional, require explicit authorization to promote the target user and a permitted target-role policy.
Validate the sanitized value against the allowlist with strict comparison using in_array( $role, $allowed, true ) before it is used
Reject disallowed values without applying a replacement role; keep nonce and per-target authorization checks before mutation.
Persist only the approved display preference; call set_role() only if an intentionally authorized role-management flow was established.
success_criteria: The posted role value is still guarded, unslashed with wp_unslash(), and sanitized with sanitize_key()
An explicit allowlist governs display-preference values or, for an intentional role-management flow, assignable roles.
Strict allowlist validation precedes persistence; role assignment, if retained, also enforces actor and target authorization.
Unauthorized requests and disallowed values leave the user role unchanged.
Members cannot gain administrator, author, or other additional privileges by tampering with a display preference.
